30	| 2026-06-11 | **NAND programming from macOS = u-boot RAM-loaded over JTAG, as a PMECC-aware flasher; the boot region needs a hand-prepended PMECC header.** New flow in [`openocd/program-nand.{sh,cfg,md}`](../openocd/program-nand.md): the init-and-stop at91bootstrap brings up DDR (as `load-ram`), then we `load_image` the at91bootstrap + `harmony.bin` + `u-boot.bin` into DDR and jump to u-boot; u-boot's `atmel_nand` (`nand erase`/`nand write`) burns NAND with PMECC. Built `u-boot.bin` from `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig` (macOS: `gmake`, OpenSSL via the **environment** so dtc's bundled-libfdt include isn't clobbered). **Validated on hardware: marvin boots standalone from NAND** (RomBOOT → at91bootstrap copies `0x100000` from `0x40000` → marvin runs, HDMI captured). | Closes the 2026-06-09 "macOS-native NAND is Phase-2 R&D" item. OpenOCD's `at91sam9` NAND driver can't do PMECC, so it can't write a bootable boot region; u-boot's driver uses the same PMECC IP and its DT (hw ECC, **8-bit/512, eccOffset 152** = `oobsize − 8·13`) matches both the chip's ONFI (`nand info`: 4096/256/8/512) and the at91bootstrap header generator — so `nand write` is RomBOOT-correct. **Two non-obvious gotchas, both bench-found:** (1) The SAM9X7 ROM reads page 0 *without ECC* expecting a NAND header — 52 copies of a 32-bit word, code at offset `0xD0` (DS60001813D p.159/162). SAM-BA's `writeboot` synthesizes this; a plain `nand write` does not, so headerless writes give RomBOOT-only (no boot). Fix: prepend the header with `binaries/make-pmecchead.sh` (wraps at91bootstrap `addpmecchead.py`) using the **real** chip params → word `0xc2605007`; *not* that script's SAM9X7 defaults (2048/64/4), which don't match this board. (2) u-boot's default `bootcmd` reads the empty kernel partition into `0x22000000`/`0x21000000`; a 3 s autoboot overwrites staged blobs with `0xff` before you can program. Fix: stage into `0x21100000`/`0x21200000` (outside its read windows) and stop autoboot on connect. QSPI path still SAM-BA (no OpenOCD driver). |

44	| 2026-05-29 | Strip queue uses 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[depth+2]` instead of pass-by-value `perf_rec_strip_t` items. | FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section (interrupts disabled). Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |

107	- **`vApplicationStackOverflowHook` is a silent infinite-loop.** ([freertos_hooks.c:62-76](../default/src/config/default/freertos_hooks.c#L62-L76)) MCC's default is `taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS()` then `for (;;)`. An actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)

With the manual-control surface adding 8 buttons and frequent press/release events during menu nav, confirm `legato_config.h` `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` has headroom for typical event bursts. Watch for Legato heap-exhaustion symptoms (silent dropped events, widget redraw glitches) once the UI is exercised on hardware.

111	- **Single-screen attach assumption for `ui/manual_input`.** `screenHide_Screen0` deletes the root widget tree, taking the Composer-generated `Screen0_*` widget pointers with it. We bind callbacks once after the first `screenShow_Screen0`. If a second Legato screen is ever added, `ManualInput_Bind` must re-run inside that screen's show path (or whichever screen owns the manual-control widgets). Not an issue today — flagged for whenever the operator UI grows beyond Screen0.

Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.

119	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.

Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
122

Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). The pin-macro generator produces `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_*` and `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_*` separately and no unified wrapper, so the MCC-emitted code fails to compile. Replace lines 162-163 (Set branch) and 169-170 (Clear branch) with explicit calls to both per-pin macros — `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set(); VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set();` and the matching Clear pair. The MCC comment in the function ("name it to 'VBUS_AH'") acknowledges the single-pin assumption.

Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.

EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. Patch: extend each check to `(... == AT_V250 || ... == NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. Two one-line OR additions. Re-apply after every USB-host MCC regen.

MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
132	     ```c
133	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
134	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
135	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
136	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
137	     ```
138	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.

140	  9. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.
141	
142	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
143	
144	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
145	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
146	
147	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
148	
149	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
150	
151	  10. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

161	- **ISC_Capture framebuffer sized for max 1920×1080 × 2 (~16 MB)** — wastes DDR at our current 720×480 use, but trivial at 256 MB total DDR and gives headroom for different sources. Reconsider if DDR becomes tight later.
162	
163	- **Retry semantics on source loss.** `app_coordinate_capture` uses a `capture_attempted` flag to prevent retry spam. On unlock it resets, so the next lock triggers a fresh Configure+Start. Untested for fast lock/unlock cycles — if the Wii toggles power, watch for state-machine glitches.

167	- **`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS` likely needs to vary by difficulty.** 220 ms tuned well on Expert (notes are dense, the delay lines up against fast-moving notes near the strike line). Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same 220 ms may strike too early. Open: per-difficulty preset, runtime-tunable from the manual-control surface, or auto-tuned from observed note-velocity. Defer until the game-state controller (spec §4.8) lands and difficulty is known to marvin — until then, expert-tuned 220 ms is the working default.

169	- **T1S link transport — direction, not yet built.** Plan to replace the FLEXCOM2 USART fretboard link with **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet + dumb PoDL** (LAN8651B1 MAC-PHY each end). System spec §6 + [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md). marvin runs **bare-metal**, so it gets *no free netdev* — it needs its own OA TC6 SPI driver. Plan: a single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared with fretboard (Cortex-A5 + Cortex-M0+). `FretboardLink_{Initialize,Send,IsConnected}` stays the public API; only the transport beneath it swaps (SPI + TC6 chunk protocol + a 14-byte L2 header wrapping the existing 17-byte/1-byte frames). marvin resources are not a concern. PoDL is dumb (fixed voltage, no SCCP) and transparent to the MCU. Decide topology (PLCA vs p2p), ethertype/MACs, and UART-fallback-during-bring-up before code lands.

176	
177	Goal: get marvin resident in the cHybrid's on-board NAND without SAM-BA. Landed it. See the decision-log entry for the full design + rationale; mechanics and runbook in [`openocd/program-nand.md`](../openocd/program-nand.md).
178	
179	- **Approach:** reuse the `load-ram` JTAG mechanism but jump to **u-boot** (built from `sam9x75_curiosity_pro_nandflash_defconfig` in `~/Projects/microchip/u-boot-mchp`) instead of marvin; u-boot's `atmel_nand` is the PMECC-aware flasher. Images are pre-staged into DDR over JTAG, then `nand erase`/`nand write` from the DBGU console (channel C, `/dev/cu.usbserial-W16_2026_4302` @115200). NAND layout: at91bootstrap @ `0x0`, `harmony.bin` @ `0x40000` (mirrors the SD/QSPI `nand_flash.bat`).
180	- **Confirmed chip (`nand info`):** page 4096, OOB 256, ECC 8-bit, sector 512 — matches the u-boot DT and the at91bootstrap header math (eccOffset 152), so the data write is RomBOOT-compatible.
181	- **First boot attempt: RomBOOT-only (no-go).** Root cause: SAM9X7 ROM needs a NAND parameter header on page 0 (read without ECC) that a plain `nand write` doesn't add. Fixed by prepending the 52×word header (`binaries/make-pmecchead.sh`, real params → `0xc2605007`, code at `0xD0`). Verified the header survived the PMECC round-trip (`md.l` of a `nand read` of page 0 → `c2605007` ×, vectors at `0xd0`).
182	- **Second gotcha:** u-boot's `bootcmd` autoboot clobbered the staged blobs at `0x22000000` with `0xff` between staging and programming. Moved staging to `0x21100000`/`0x21200000` and stop autoboot on console connect.
183	- **Validated on hardware:** power-cycle (JP3 NAND in, JP4 QSPI out, no SD) → `RomBOOT` → `AT91Bootstrap 4.0.13` → `NAND: Copy 0x100000 bytes from 0x40000 to 0x23f00000` → marvin up (fretboard link, pipeline, TC358743 detected 720x480p@60, ISC capture armed). Bit-exact app verify (`cmp.b` 517328 B same).
184	- **Artifacts (all in-repo, self-contained):** `binaries/sam9x7-nandflashboot-uboot-4.0.13-pmecchead.bin` (headed bootstrap) + `make-pmecchead.sh` generator (no external-tree dep); the flasher `binaries/sam9x75-uboot-nandflash-flasher-2025.07.bin` (built from <https://github.com/linux4microchip/u-boot-mchp> `linux4microchip-2026.04`; build recipe in `binaries/README.md`); `openocd/program-nand.{sh,cfg,md}`, `openocd/erase-nand.{sh,cfg}`, and the shared `openocd/nand_console.py`. `openocd/README.md` "Scope" updated (NAND-from-macOS no longer R&D).

1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed. |
43	| Lightweight log shim, FreeRTOS analytics, task priorities | ✅ done. |
44	| CV detection pipeline | 🚧 M1 complete: `cv_marvin_v1` running on captured frames, `detector_state_t` bus active. No actuation path through detector yet. §4.2. |
45	| Fretboard link (FLEXCOM2 USART) | ✅ working; gameplay tested over the original USB CDC host link. Link rewired to a direct FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board (no host-capable USB port); pending on-hardware re-validation. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
47	| Operator UI (Legato) | 🚧 Manual-control surface (8 buttons, Legato Composer) done; full calibration/log UI not started. §4.5, open Q5. |
48	| Reference-data recording & export (SD) | 🚧 SD recording not started. Perf-log USB CDC export (separate dev-tooling path) complete at 2.77 MB/s. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 Partial: logging, FreeRTOS analytics, static task priorities done; config persistence and watchdog not started. §4.7. |
50	| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 not started. §4.8, open Q10/Q11. |

101	   │   cmd RX ──► open-drain GPIO       │                       │   │
102	   │   (frets PA01–07, strums PA00/03)  │                       │   │
103	   └─────────────────┬──────────────────┘                       │   │
104	                     │ open-drain GPIO                          │   │
105	                     ▼                                          │   │
106	   ┌────────────────────────────────────┐                       │   │
107	   │ Wii Guitar Hero controller         │                       │   │
108	   │ (5 frets + strum bar)              │◄──────────────────────┘   │
109	   └────────────────┬───────────────────┘                           │
110	                    │ controller cable                              │
111	                    ▼                                               │
112	            (back to Wii) ◄────────────────────────────────────────┘
113	
114	                        ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
115	                        │ optional dev PC (fret-tuner)    │
116	                        │ ─ calibration / tuning UI       │
117	                        │ ─ replay / detector comparison  │
118	                        │ ─ training-data ingest          │
119	                        └─────────────────────────────────┘
120	                          (off-band; not in runtime path)
121	```
122	
123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.
163

201	
202	## 4. Subsystems
203	
204	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
205	
206	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
207	
208	**What this subsystem owns:**
209	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
210	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
211	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
212	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
213	
214	**What it doesn't own:**
215	- CV processing (§4.2).
216	- Recording / export (§4.6).
217	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
218	
219	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
220	
221	#### 4.2.1 Role
222	
223	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
224	
225	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
226	
227	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
228	
229	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
230	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
231	
232	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
233	
234	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
235	
236	```
237	typedef struct {
238	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
239	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
240	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
241	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
242	    struct {
243	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
244	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
245	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
246	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
247	} detector_state_t;
248	```
249	
250	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
251	
252	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
253	
254	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
255	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
256	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
257	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
258	
259	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
260	
261	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
262	
263	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
264	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
265	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
266	
267	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
268	
269	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
270	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
271	
272	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
273	
274	Direct **FLEXCOM2 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM2 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads.
275	
276	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM2_USART_Write`.
277	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM2 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
278	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
279	
280	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
281	
282	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
283	
284	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
285	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
286	- Per-fret release scheduling.
287	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
288	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
289	
290	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
291	
292	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
293	
294	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
295	
296	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
297	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
298	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
299	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
300	
301	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
302	
303	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
304	
305	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
306	
307	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
308	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
309	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
310	
311	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
312	
313	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
314	
315	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
316	
317	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
318	
319	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
320	
321	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
322	
323	```
324	recordings/
325	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
326	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
327	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
328	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
329	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
330	    └── keyframes/
331	        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
332	        ├── 000060.bgr
333	        └── ...
334	```
335	
336	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
337	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
338	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 12-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~2.9 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
339	- **Keyframes** — raw BGR888 packed dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 × 3 B = 1.04 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.04 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~312 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
340	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
341	
342	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
343	
344	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
345	
346	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
347	
348	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
349	
350	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
351	
352	Minimum fields:
353	
354	```json
355	{
356	  "schema_version": 1,
357	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
358	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
359	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGR888" },
360	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
361	  "detectors": [
362	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
363	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
364	  ],
365	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
366	  "ended_utc": null
367	}
368	```
369	
370	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
371	
372	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
373	
374	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
375	
376	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
377	
378	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
379	
380	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
381	
382	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
383	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
384	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
385	
386	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
387	
388	### 4.7 System services 🚧
389	
390	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
391	
392	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
393	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
394	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
395	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
396	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
397	
398	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
399	
400	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
401	
402	#### 4.8.1 Role
403	
404	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
405	
406	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
407	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
408	
409	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
410	
411	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
412	
413	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
414	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
415	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
416	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
417	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
418	
419	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
420	
421	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
422	
423	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
424	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
425	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
426	
427	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
428	
429	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
430	
431	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
432	
433	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
434	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
435	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
436	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
437	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
438	
439	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
440	
441	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
442	
443	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
444	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
445	
446	---
447	
448	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
449	
450	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
451	
452	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
453	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
454	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).
455	
456	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
457	
458	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
459	
460	| Toggle | Effect |
461	|---|---|
462	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
463	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
464	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
465	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
466	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
467	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
468	
469	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.
470	
471	## 7. Build & deploy 🚧
472	
473	To be filled. Topics: MCC-clobbered files (which paths are safe to edit by hand vs. regenerate), `user.cmake` boundaries, flashing workflow, sequence of MCC steps to reproduce the project.
474	
475	## 8. Phasing & milestones 🚧
476	
477	Proposed order; each is a buildable demo:
478	
479	1. **M1 — Reference detector v0** (§4.2). One CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` to the bus. No actuation. Proves the bus and the detection task structure.
480	2. **M2 — Fretboard link** (§4.3). UART up; ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus alongside `cv_marvin_v1`.
481	3. **M3 — Timing pipeline + actuation** (§4.4). Chord FIFO + strum scheduling; commands sent over UART; fretboard actuates. End-to-end play possible.
482	4. **M4 — Recording to SD** (§4.6). SDMMC + FAT mount; record task writes state/commands/ADC/keyframes during a session.
483	5. **M5 — Operator UI v0** (§4.5). Live view with overlays; mode toggles. UI framework decided here.
484	6. **M6 — Calibration UI** (§4.5). Per-fret ROI placement + threshold tuning on the device.
485	7. **M7 — Replay** (§6). Load a recording from SD, replay through the timing pipeline.
486	8. **M8 — Standalone-fretboard fallback** (§4.4). Marvin-disabled-pipeline mode validated.
487	9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). Recognize main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score states; surface as `xGameStateQueue` events. No control yet.
488	10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). High-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
489	
490	Live-stream Ethernet, Edge-AI integration, and config-on-flash are post-M8.

20	/* USB-device CDC ACM sink. The MCC config provides USB_DEVICE_Initialize
21	 * + the USB_DEVICE_Tasks worker; we own the application-side state
22	 * machine: open the device handle, register event handlers, attach
23	 * on VBUS, and provide a write API for the perf-log drain task.
24	 *
25	 * Single producer (the drain task). Not thread-safe by design: a second
26	 * writer would race on s_tx_head and could allocate the same ring slot
27	 * twice. */
28	
29	/* Header(6) + max payload (sizeof perf_rec_strip_t) + CRC(2), padded up
30	 * to a cache-line multiple so UDPHS DMA can't share a line with whatever
31	 * sits next to us in BSS. Derived from PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES so the two
32	 * constants can't drift — a too-small sink buffer silently rejects
33	 * larger strips at the size check, accumulating dropped_sink. */
34	#define SINK_FRAME_BYTES_RAW  (6u + PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES + 2u)
35	#define SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX  ((SINK_FRAME_BYTES_RAW + 63u) & ~63u)
36	
37	/* Depth of the staging ring. Three independent capacities must all
38	 * permit N concurrent in-flight writes:
39	 *   - this ring depth                                       (here)
40	 *   - CDC per-instance queueSizeWrite                       (usb_device_init_data.c via MCC yml)
41	 *   - USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED minus RX/notif use (configuration.h via MCC yml)
42	 * MCC config has all three sized for N=3; bump together if changed. */
43	#define SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH    3u
44	
45	#define SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS    50u
46	#define SINK_CONFIG_WAIT_MS   100u
47	#define SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS 100u
48	
49	static USB_DEVICE_HANDLE       s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID;
50	static volatile bool           s_is_configured;
51	static volatile USB_CDC_LINE_CODING s_line_coding =
52	{
53	    .dwDTERate   = 921600u,
54	    .bCharFormat = 0u,
55	    .bParityType = 0u,
56	    .bDataBits   = 8u,
57	};
58	static volatile USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE s_cls;
59	
60	/* Counting semaphore: tokens = ring slots free for the producer to fill.
61	 * Init = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH (all slots free). Take before claiming a
62	 * slot; ISR gives one back per WRITE_COMPLETE. */
63	static SemaphoreHandle_t s_tx_credits;
64	static StaticSemaphore_t s_tx_credits_buf;
65	
66	/* Staging ring for outgoing frames. UDPHS DMAs from these addresses;
67	 * keeping the outer array CACHE_ALIGN with SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX a
68	 * multiple of CACHE_LINE_SIZE keeps every inner buffer line-aligned
69	 * so the driver's cache-maintenance ops don't collide with neighbors.
70	 * s_tx_head advances one slot per accepted submission; producer is the
71	 * single drain task so no lock is needed. */
72	static uint8_t CACHE_ALIGN s_tx_ring[SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH][SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX];
73	static uint32_t s_tx_head;
74	
75	/* RX staging — one bulk-OUT max-packet at HS (512 B). Must be ≥ MPS or
76	 * the UDPHS driver rejects the IRP / drops the packet. Cache-aligned for
77	 * the same reason as s_tx_ring. */
78	#define SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES  512u
79	static uint8_t CACHE_ALIGN s_rx_buf[SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES];
80	
81	static void prime_rx_read(void)
82	{
83	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
84	    (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0, &th,
85	                              s_rx_buf, SINK_RX_BUF_BYTES);
86	}
87	
88	/* Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF). USB hardware already CRCs every
89	 * bulk packet on the wire, so this checksum's job is *framing-layer*
90	 * detection only — false SOF matches during resync, firmware bugs that
91	 * write a wrong LEN or a partial frame. Fletcher catches single-byte
92	 * changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536
93	 * accidental-match rate against random byte streams — plenty for that
94	 * job, at ~2 cycles/byte vs ~6 for a table-driven CRC-16. Block-mod
95	 * pattern from RFC 1146 / Wikipedia: defer the modulo until uint32
96	 * could overflow, which gives ~5800 iterations between reductions. */
97	static uint16_t fletcher16(uint16_t init, const uint8_t *p, uint16_t len)
98	{
99	    uint32_t s1 = (uint32_t)(init & 0xFFu);
100	    uint32_t s2 = (uint32_t)((init >> 8) & 0xFFu);
101	
102	    while (len > 0u)
103	    {
104	        uint16_t blk = (len > 5802u) ? 5802u : len;
105	        len = (uint16_t)(len - blk);
106	        do
107	        {
108	            s1 += *p++;
109	            s2 += s1;
110	            blk--;
111	        } while (blk > 0u);
112	        s1 %= 255u;
113	        s2 %= 255u;
114	    }
115	
116	    return (uint16_t)((s2 << 8) | s1);
117	}

119	/* ─── CDC class event handler ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
120	
121	static USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE cdc_event_handler(
122	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX index,
123	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT event,
124	    void *pData,
125	    uintptr_t userData)
126	{
127	    (void)index;
128	    (void)userData;
129	
130	    switch (event)
131	    {
132	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_GET_LINE_CODING:
133	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlSend(s_dev_handle,
134	                                         (void *)&s_line_coding,
135	                                         sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
136	            break;
137	
138	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_LINE_CODING:
139	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlReceive(s_dev_handle,
140	                                            (void *)&s_line_coding,
141	                                            sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
142	            break;
143	
144	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE:
145	        {
146	            const USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE *cls = pData;
147	            s_cls.dtr     = cls->dtr;
148	            s_cls.carrier = cls->carrier;
149	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
150	                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
151	            break;
152	        }
153	
154	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SEND_BREAK:
155	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
156	                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
157	            break;
158	
159	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_RECEIVED:
160	            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
161	                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
162	            break;
163	
164	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
165	        {
166	            /* One ring slot has cleared the wire — return its credit. */
167	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
168	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_tx_credits, &hpw);
169	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
170	            break;
171	        }
172	
173	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE:
174	        {
175	            const USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_READ_COMPLETE *rd = pData;
176	            if (rd != NULL && rd->status == USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_OK
177	                && rd->length > 0u)
178	            {
179	                PerfLogRx_Feed(s_rx_buf, (uint32_t)rd->length);
180	            }
181	            prime_rx_read();
182	            break;
183	        }
184	
185	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_SENT:
186	        default:
187	            break;
188	    }
189	    return USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;
190	}

194	static void device_event_handler(USB_DEVICE_EVENT event, void *eventData,
195	                                 uintptr_t context)
196	{
197	    (void)context;
198	
199	    switch (event)
200	    {
201	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
202	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DECONFIGURED:
203	            s_is_configured = false;
204	            break;
205	
206	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED:
207	        {
208	            const USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED *cd = eventData;
209	            if (cd->configurationValue == 1u)
210	            {
211	                (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_EventHandlerSet(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
212	                                                    cdc_event_handler, 0u);
213	                s_is_configured = true;
214	                LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device CDC configured\r\n");
215	                prime_rx_read();
216	            }
217	            break;
218	        }
219	
220	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
221	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
222	            break;
223	
224	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
225	            (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
226	            s_is_configured = false;
227	            break;
228	
229	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
230	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
231	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
232	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
233	        default:
234	            break;
235	    }
236	}

238	/* ─── Public sink interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
239	
240	void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
241	{
242	    s_tx_credits = xSemaphoreCreateCountingStatic(SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH,
243	                                                  SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH,
244	                                                  &s_tx_credits_buf);
245	    configASSERT(s_tx_credits != NULL);
246	
247	    PerfLogRx_Initialize();
248	
249	    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
250	     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
251	     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
252	    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
253	    {
254	        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
255	                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
256	        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
257	        {
258	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS));
259	        }
260	    }
261	
262	    USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(s_dev_handle, device_event_handler, 0u);
263	
264	    /* Cold-boot-with-cable case: by the time we register the handler the
265	     * UDPHS driver may have already raced past the VBUS edge it needed
266	     * to fire POWER_DETECTED, or the host may have seen a brief pull-up
267	     * assertion during early boot and given up retrying. Force a clean
268	     * detach→short delay→attach edge so the host sees an unambiguous
269	     * device-arrival on the bus. Hot-plug after this point is unaffected
270	     * because POWER_REMOVED/POWER_DETECTED still drive Detach/Attach. */
271	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
272	    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(100));
273	    (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
274	
275	    LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device opened, waiting for host enumeration\r\n");
276	}
277	
278	bool PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected(void)
279	{
280	    return s_is_configured && s_cls.dtr;
281	}
282	
283	void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len)
284	{
285	    if (!s_is_configured || !s_cls.dtr)
286	    {
287	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
288	        return;
289	    }
290	
291	    uint16_t total = (uint16_t)(6u + len + 2u);
292	    if (total > SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX)
293	    {
294	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
295	        return;
296	    }
297	
298	    /* Wait for a free ring slot. With N=3 against the lower CDC layer's
299	     * 3-deep transfer queue, this only blocks when the host has stalled
300	     * — under load the producer pipelines at the rate ISR returns
301	     * credits. Timeout drops the record and lets the next sink state-
302	     * machine pass observe DECONFIGURED if the host went away. */
303	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_tx_credits,
304	                       pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
305	    {
306	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
307	        return;
308	    }
309	
310	    uint8_t *frame = s_tx_ring[s_tx_head];
311	
312	    frame[0] = 0x55u;
313	    frame[1] = 0x4Du;
314	    frame[2] = 0x52u;
315	    frame[3] = 0x56u;
316	    frame[4] = (uint8_t)(len & 0xFFu);
317	    frame[5] = (uint8_t)((len >> 8) & 0xFFu);
318	    memcpy(&frame[6], payload, len);
319	
320	    uint16_t fcs = fletcher16(0xFFFFu, &frame[4], (uint16_t)(2u + len));
321	    frame[6u + len]      = (uint8_t)(fcs & 0xFFu);
322	    frame[6u + len + 1u] = (uint8_t)((fcs >> 8) & 0xFFu);
323	
324	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
325	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT r = USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
326	                                                  &th,
327	                                                  frame, total,
328	                                                  USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
329	    if (r != USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_OK)
330	    {
331	        /* Submission rejected: ISR won't fire for this slot, so hand
332	         * the credit back ourselves. Slot stays free; head doesn't
333	         * advance. */
334	        (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_tx_credits);
335	        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
336	        return;
337	    }
338	
339	    s_tx_head = (s_tx_head + 1u) % SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH;
340	}

299	static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
300	{
301	    (void)param;
302	
303	    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
304	    register_post_scheduler_tasks();
305	    s_running = true;
306	
307	    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
308	    bool prev_connected = false;
309	
310	    for (;;)
311	    {
312	        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
313	        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
314	        {
315	            emit_session_record();
316	        }
317	        prev_connected = now_connected;
318	
319	        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
320	        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
321	                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
322	        {
323	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
324	            /* Drain all currently queued state records before moving on.
325	             * Strips cost ~5 ms apiece on the wire, so a one-state-per-
326	             * iteration loop runs at ~50 Hz under load — well below the
327	             * ~700 stamps/s production rate. Same shape as the strip
328	             * drain below. */
329	            while (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec, 0) == pdTRUE)
330	            {
331	                PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
332	            }
333	        }
334	
335	        /* Strip drain: dequeue slot index, write the slot's data via
336	         * pointer (no copy), return slot to the free pool. */
337	        uint8_t slot_idx;
338	        while (xQueueReceive(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) == pdTRUE)
339	        {
340	            const perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
341	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));
342	            (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
343	        }
344	
345	        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
346	        {
347	            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
348	            emit_drop_record();
349	            sample_and_emit_hwms();
350	            sample_and_emit_runtimes();
351	        }
352	    }
353	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-12 01:12:16Z)**_

Key finding: **FLEXCOM1 was generated in plain blocking/polled mode** — the header exposes only `Write/Read/WriteByte/TransmitterIsReady/TransmitComplete`, no callbacks, no ring-buffer count API, no DMA. Let me confirm the baud it was set to, contrast against FLEXCOM2's ring-buffer API, and get the record sizes/rates that drive the throughput math.

I've got the full picture now. Here's my analysis — the good news is the previous USB→UART move (fretboard link) and the perf-log's existing sink abstraction make this mostly a "write one new sink file" job.

## What's already in our favor

- **The sink is a clean seam.** [perf_log.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c) only ever calls three functions — `PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize`, `PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed`, `PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected` ([perf_log_sink.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink.h)). The framing (SOF `55 4D 52 56` + u16 LEN + payload + Fletcher-16) lives entirely inside the sink. Swap the sink body; the drain task, records, and framing are untouched.
- **The host is already transport-agnostic.** [transport.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/transport.py) is pyserial reading a serial device with the same frame parser. CDC ACM *ignored* baud; FTDI channel D will *not* — host just needs the right `/dev/cu.usbserial-…D` path and matching baud.

## What MCC generated, decoded

FLEXCOM1 is currently in **plain blocking mode** — the header only exposes `Write/Read/WriteByte/TransmitterIsReady/TransmitComplete`, no callbacks, no ring-count API. Baud is `BRGR = CD(2)|FP(6)`, OVER=0 → 266.667 MHz / (16 × 2.75) = **6.06 Mbaud** (≈ FT4232H's 12M/2 = 6.0M; 1% mismatch, well inside 8N1 tolerance). At 8N1 that's **600 KB/s** on the wire.

## My recommendations

**1. Mode: ring-buffer, *with* the hardware FIFO enabled.** Mirror what fretboard_link did for FLEXCOM2 TX — `WriteFramed` becomes a `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write()` copy-and-return, backpressure via `WriteFreeBufferCountGet()`. This deletes the whole USB credit-semaphore dance.

**2. On the FIFO — yes, enable it, and this is the part to watch.** I checked the in-tree FLEXCOM2 ring plib ([plib_flexcom2_usart.c:66-67,714-715](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/peripheral/flexcom/usart/plib_flexcom2_usart.c)): as generated it interrupts on **TXRDY = THR-empty = one IRQ per byte** — the `wrThreshold`/`rdThreshold` it references are *software-ring* notification thresholds, not the hardware FIFO. So plain ring-buffer mode is exactly the "interrupt on every character" case you're worried about (600K IRQ/s at 6 Mbaud). The FIFO checkbox is what flips the generated ISR to refill up to FIFO-depth per interrupt (`FIFOEN` + `TXFTHRES`), cutting IRQ rate by ~depth×. **So: enable FIFO, then verify the regenerated ISR actually uses `FLEX_US_CR_FIFOEN` + threshold, not bare TXRDY.** The FIFO is 6-bit-level (`FLEX_US_FLR.TXFL`, mask 0x3F) — depth is 16 or 32, confirm in the DS. Either is plenty: the FIFO is only an interrupt-coalescing stage; the multi-KB software ring does the real buffering.

**3. DMA: not worth it.** The "don't interrupt per char" instinct is right, but FIFO already solves it, and our *real* byte rate is tiny. The records that fit are dominated by ~700 STAMP/s (~20 KB/s steady-state; ~40 KB/s even with DETECTOR/TIMING/FRETBOARD_RAW on) — that's ~400 Kbit/s into a 6 Mbit pipe, 15× headroom, and only a few K IRQ/s once the FIFO batches. DMA on the Harmony FLEXCOM USART isn't a turnkey ring plib anyway — you'd hand-roll XDMAC descriptors or fall back to single-shot writes needing a SW queue on top (i.e. reinventing what we'd delete). Keep DMA in your back pocket *only* if profiling later shows TX-ISR jitter polluting the timing measurements — but FIFO-batched ring should stay well under that.

## Two things that genuinely change semantics

**Bandwidth ceiling.** 600 KB/s wire vs USB's measured 2.77 MB/s. Everything fits **except STRIP records** (pixel data, up to 65 KB each — that's what drove the 2.77 MB/s). Strips simply cannot stream over this link in real time. They're already default-disabled; my recommendation is to accept they're a USB-era luxury and keep them off on the UART path (the size check in `WriteFramed` will drop+account them if a host enables them anyway).

**Loss of "is anyone listening?" + flow control.** USB CDC gave us DTR-gating (`IsConnected` → don't spew when no terminal; rising edge re-emits SESSION so a reconnect sees the schema) and implicit host backpressure. A bare TX UART into FTDI has neither — marvin can't tell if anything's attached, and the wire always "succeeds." I'd propose:
- **Free-run** the sink (subject to the type mask), drop the DTR concept. Continuous TX on a dedicated FTDI channel is harmless.
- Replace the DTR rising-edge SESSION re-emit with: **emit SESSION on any valid received command frame** (host already sends `set-mask` on attach via the existing RX path) plus a low-rate periodic SESSION. That restores "reconnect always sees the schema" without a modem line.
- Backpressure stays as drop-on-full at ring enqueue → existing `PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop` accounting, same as today's credit-timeout drop.

---

Net: a new `perf_log_sink_flexcom.c` implementing the same three-function interface, ring+FIFO writes, free-run with RX-triggered SESSION; host gets a one-line port (device path + 6 Mbaud, drop the DTR assumption).
